result.summary: Converts `building-on` in `contrib/guix/toolchains.scm` from an eagerly evaluated variable into a procedure called during derivation lowering. This ensures the `--build` flag uses the architecture passed via Guix's `--system` flag rather than the architecture of the host executing `guix shell`.
result.problem: When running Guix with `--system` on a different host architecture under emulation (for example, `--system=aarch64-linux` on an x86_64 machine), `guix shell` loads the manifest before applying `--system`. As a result, `(%current-system)` evaluates to the host's architecture at module load time, generating a mismatched `--build=x86_64-guix-linux-gnu` flag that causes `gcc-cross-sans-libc` to fail during configuration.
evidence: PR description documents configure error on master: 'checking for CET support... configure: error: compiler and assembler with CET support are required for --enable-cet'

PR description verifies derivation equivalence: native builds produce identical derivations on master and with this PR, confirming release builds are unaffected while correcting emulated cross-system builds

result.card: Converts `building-on` in `contrib/guix/toolchains.scm` from an eagerly evaluated variable into a procedure evaluated during derivation lowering. When running Guix with `--system` under emulation on a foreign host (such as an aarch64 build on x86_64), `(%current-system)` previously evaluated at module load time before `--system` took effect, generating an incorrect `--build` triplet that failed `gcc-cross-sans-libc` configuration. Derivations for native release builds remain identical.

risk.why: A mistake in Guix toolchain definitions could alter compiler build derivations or break release binary reproducibility.
